title: Kanban is a System: 5 Design Decisions
summary: This lesson breaks down five critical UX decisions for designing effective Kanban boards, focusing on interaction feedback, layout stability, and information density.

transcript.text: Kanban is a system. One drag. Five decisions behind it.
Decision one: the drag preview lifts. A shadow and a three-degree tilt. Trello tilts its cards the same way. The tilt says the card is in your hand.
Decision two: the drop placeholder is the exact size of the card. The column opens once, then nothing else moves. A thin line makes every card below jump when it lands.
Decision three: WIP limits live on the column header. In progress: four of four. Hit the limit and the header turns amber. The board says stop before the manager does.
Decision four: columns collapse to a vertical label with a count. Done: 42. Horizontal scroll is the failure mode. If you scroll sideways, you lost the board.
Decision five: swimlanes before a second board. Split rows by team or priority. Same columns, same flow. Two boards means two truths.

Five decisions. One board the whole team can trust. Now make Claude Code think like a senior UX designer. UX Engine designs a screen before coding, audits what is broken, reviews the diff, and kills the AI look. Link in bio.

design_principles: Preventing Layout Shift (CLS) using sized placeholders
Information density management (collapsing columns vs. horizontal scrolling)
Single Source of Truth (swimlanes vs. multiple boards)
before_after: Demonstrates the difference between a 'thin line' placeholder (causing layout jump) versus a 'sized slot' (zero layout shift).
